name: Benjamin Contee
bio: A Delegate and a Representative from Maryland; born at "Brookefield," near Nottingham, Prince George's County, Md., in 1755; attended a private school; served in the Revolutionary War, lieutenant and later captain in the Third Maryland Battalion; member of the Maryland house of delegates, 1785-1787; Delegate to the Confederation Congress in 1788; elected as an Anti-Administration candidate to the First Congress (March 4, 1789-March 3, 1791); was not a candidate for renomination to the 2nd Congress in 1790; traveled in various European countries, and studied theology; continued theological study on his return to the United States, and ordained a minister of the Episcopal Church in 1803;  pastor of the Episcopal Church at Port Tobacco, Charles County; was serving as presiding judge of the Charles County Orphans' Court at the time of his death in 1815; died on November 30, 1815, in Charles County, Md.; interment at "Bromont," his former home, near Port Tobacco, Md.
